text: In ML Drift's GetTensorDescForValue, when CalculationsPrecision is kF16 or kF32F16 every graph value of type FLOAT32 gets a FLOAT16 tensor on the GPU, except values that are graph outputs produced by a CAST; with kF32 the original types are kept.

LiteRT-LM's compiled-model executor (agello-next) uses ActivationDataType FLOAT16 unless the executor settings set another type, and CreateCompilationOptions sets LiteRT GPU precision kFp16 for any activation type other than FLOAT32.

LiteRT's Metal ML Drift delegate maps its precision option kFp16 to CalculationsPrecision::kF16 and kFp32 to kF32, maps kDefault to kF16 when the GPU supports round-to-nearest (else kF32F16), and forces kF32F16 when use_f32_accum_for_fp16 is set.

ML Drift's GetRecommendedMaxTotalSpatialSize returns 16 for an Apple GPU at kF16 precision (8 at kF32): the largest number of rows a fully connected node handles before ML Drift switches to a convolution.
formula: base 4; x2 for kF16; x2 for any GPU that is not Mali; x2 only for Adreno gen 7+; capped at 16: Apple kF16 = 4*2*2 = 16, kF32 = 4*2 = 8

On Apple GPUs at kF16, E4B's weight products in decode (1 row) and verify (4 rows) stay under ML Drift's 16-row limit and run in the FullyConnected kernel, while prefill_128 (128 rows) and prefill_1024 (1,024 rows) exceed it and run as convolutions.

text: Above the fully connected row limit, ML Drift runs INT4 weights as an INT4 convolution only with ModelHints::kAllow4bitConvs and SupportsConvGenericInt4 (OpenCL with cl_intel_subgroup_matrix_multiply_accumulate), and runs INT4 or INT8 weights through FullyConnectedInt8QuantizedWithSrcQuantization only when the weights are not group-quantized, carry precomputed sums (sum_i), SupportsConvolutionInt8 holds and kDisallow8bitConvs is not set; otherwise it uses FullyConnectedSrcFloatExternalWeightsWithConversion.

On Apple GPUs (Metal), ML Drift's SupportsConvolutionInt8 is true only when SupportsConvAppleMPP is: its other tests need cl_arm_matrix_multiply (Mali), wave memory on Adreno/Intel/PowerVR, OpenCL/WebGPU/Vulkan dot-product support (ConvGeneric), or Nvidia/Intel INT8 wave-matrix ops.

ML Drift's SupportsConvAppleMPP(gpu_info) requires the Metal API, an Apple GPU, ML Drift family Apple10 or later and Metal Shading Language 4.0 or later; ConvAppleMPP is therefore never selected on Apple7, Apple8 or Apple9 GPUs.

LiteRT-LM (agello-next) enables LiteRT's AllowSrcQuantizedFcConvOps GPU option unless AdvancedSettings.allow_src_quantized_fc_conv_ops is set to false, and the ML Drift delegate adds ModelHints::kDisallow8bitConvs only when that option is off, so by default ML Drift may run quantized-activation INT8 convolutions for the LLM.

ML Drift's Quantize node (named quantize_<source type>_to_<packed type>) quantizes each spatial position of the activations (one token row) asymmetrically from that row's own minimum and maximum, rounding to the packed integer range, and keeps the per-row parameters in an FP32 tensor; on an Apple10 GPU with SupportsConvAppleMPP the packed type is kInt8C4.

On Apple10, FullyConnectedInt8QuantizedWithSrcQuantization selects ConvAppleMPP's INT8 variant (CreateConvAppleMPPInt8) with an INT32 intermediate result and a fused dequantization to the activation type, and adds a WeightsConversion node named weights_convert_<source>_to_<destination> when the weights' layout or type differ; for E4B these are weights_convert_uint4_to_int8 (163 INT4 tensors) and weights_convert_uint8_to_int8 (47 INT8 tensors) in each prefill graph.

text: ML Drift's INT8-path dequantization runs in FP32: the INT32 accumulator times weights_scale times the row's source scale, plus weights_scale times the source zero point times the precomputed weight sums, plus zero-point terms when the weights have zero points.

In FullyConnectedSrcFloatExternalWeightsWithConversion, ML Drift estimates conversion_cost = 100 x (source weight bytes + converted FP16 weight bytes) / FLOPs x flops_per_byte, with flops_per_byte 110 when the ConvAppleMPP path applies and 32 on other Apple GPUs, and reads the original weights in a single convolution only when that cost exceeds 20 and the weights are not ringed; otherwise it adds a separate weights_convert node, which the builder's comment treats as a cost of every run.
formula: conversion_cost = 100 * (src_bytes + dst_bytes) / flops * flops_per_byte; single convolution when conversion_cost > 20

text: For E4B's INT4 weight products on Apple7 to Apple9 GPUs, ML Drift's conversion cost is 3.9 at 1,024 rows (so it converts the weights to FP16 first) and 31.25 at 128 rows (so the convolution reads INT4 directly); for INT8 weights it is 4.69 and 37.5, matching the 163 weights_convert_uint4_to_float16 nodes in prefill_1024 and none in prefill_128 on the simulated Apple9/8/7 runs.

text: ConvAppleMPP reads external weights directly only in layout kOSpatialIOGroupI4O4, and LiteRT's runtime_bmm parser gives the K cache of a query-key product layout kOSpatialIOGroupO4I4 and the V cache of a probability-value product kOSpatialIOGroupI4O4; so in E4B's prefill_128 on Apple10 the 23 value products read the INT8 V cache directly while the 23 key products convert K to FP16 first, and in prefill_1024 all 46 convert.

text: FullyConnectedSrcFloatExternalWeightsWithConversion tries, in order: ConvAppleMPP reading the original weights (if a single convolution is recommended and ConvAppleMPP supports them), ConvWaveMatrix reading them, ConvGeneric reading them (supported only on OpenCL Intel GPUs at kF16), ConvAppleMPP with converted FP16 weights (if use_apple_mpp), and finally SelectConvolutionWithExternalWeights.

ML Drift sets use_apple_mpp in FullyConnectedSrcFloatExternalWeightsWithConversion only when SupportsConvAppleMPP holds, the convolution precision is kF16 and the source has a multiple of 32 channels, and then copies a source without a softmax input to the DHWBCC4 buffer layout.

On Apple GPUs, SelectConvolutionWithExternalWeights delegates to SelectConvolutionExternalWeightsApple, which builds ConvWaveMatrix when SupportsConvWaveMatrix and IsGoodTaskSizeForAppleConvSimd hold and ConvGeneric otherwise.
ML Drift's FullyConnected kernel accumulates in FP16 when the precision is kF16, in FP32 otherwise, and in INT32 when its source tensor is INT8.

ML Drift's FullyConnected kernel unpacks quantized weights as unsigned 2-, 4- or 8-bit fields and dequantizes each as w = u x scale - scale x (shift + zero_point), with shift 2, 8 and 128 for INT2, INT4 and INT8: the stored values are offset by half the range.
ML Drift's fc::GetDataTypeForWeights maps weight descriptors of type kUint8, kUint4 and kUint2 to the FullyConnected weight types kInt8, kInt4 and kInt2.

When a FullyConnected node has a softmax input (the probability-value product after LiteRT's bounded-attention rewrite), the kernel turns each source logit v into a probability as exp(v - max) x (1 / sum) from the reduction tensor, in the activation type (FP16 at kF16).

On Apple GPUs with Metal, ML Drift sizes the FullyConnected work group by output slices per compute unit, splitting the reduction over 1 to 128 threads in y, with 256 threads per group on GPUs with at least 16 compute units and 128 otherwise.

With a dst_end_ch_index runtime check, ML Drift's FullyConnected kernel computes only output slices below the end read from the params buffer (rounded up by GetRuntimeEndSlice), and with a src_end_ch_index it stops the reduction at (params[src_end_ch_index] + 3) / 4 slices.

ML Drift's ConvAppleMPP kernel includes MetalPerformancePrimitives and runs mpp::tensor_ops::matmul2d over 4 simdgroups (128 threads per threadgroup), with tiles of 64 rows by 128 output channels by default (64 when the output channels are not a multiple of 128, and always 64 in the variant that reads I4O4 external weights directly) and a 32-channel K tile when it tiles K itself.
ConvAppleMPP's matmul2d accumulates into a cooperative tensor of the destination's scalar type: FP16 for its floating-point (attention) uses at kF16 and INT32 for the INT8 weight products.

When ConvAppleMPP reads I4O4 external weights itself, it dequantizes uint8, uint4 or uint2 weights to half with the scale and bias before the matmul, and for an INT8 weight type it turns offset uint4 nibbles into signed INT8 by XOR with 0x8 and sign extension.
With a softmax input, ConvAppleMPP reads the source manually and turns logits into probabilities as exp(src - max) x (1 / sum) in half before staging them in threadgroup memory.
A comment in ML Drift's GpuModelBuilder gives about 110 FLOPs per byte for 'M5/A19, GPUs with NA' (Neural Accelerators) and about 32 for 'M4/A18 and below, GPUs without NA'.

On Apple GPUs, ML Drift's SupportsConvWaveMatrix requires an 8x8x8 wave matrix multiply in the precision's type at kF32 or kF16 (not kF32F16), an even number of input slices and a multiple of 4 output slices; the external-weights variant also requires Metal, layout kOSpatialIOGroupI4O4 and float32, float16, uint8, uint4 or uint2 weights.

ML Drift's Metal environment registers 8x8x8 FLOAT16 and FLOAT32 wave matrix multiplies (and BFLOAT16 with native bfloat support) only when the device supports Metal Shading Language 2.3 or later and its ML Drift family is Apple7 or later.
On Metal, ML Drift lowers its ucl::wave_matrix type to simdgroup_matrix<type, rows, cols> and ucl::WaveMatrixMAC to simdgroup_multiply_accumulate.

ConvWaveMatrix accumulates in FP16 when its weights type is floating point and the precision is kF16, in FP32 at other float precisions, and in INT32 or UINT32 for integer weights types; with external weights it sets the weights type from the precision, so E4B's prefill products accumulate in FP16 on Apple7 to Apple9.

ML Drift's IsGoodTaskSizeForAppleConvSimd accepts a convolution for ConvWaveMatrix when the rows fill 32-wide waves to at least 75% on Apple9 (95% on other families), there are at least 16 waves per compute unit at FP16 (8 at FP32), and each thread does at least 512 FLOPs on Apple9 (2,048 elsewhere).
With a softmax input, ConvWaveMatrix turns each source value into a probability as exp(src - max) x (1 / sum) before the matrix multiply.
No E4B graph node runs ConvGeneric (conv_generic) on Apple M6 or on the simulated A17 Pro, M2 and M1, at the agello-next pins.

text: LiteRT's runtime_bmm parser turns an odml.runtime_bmm composite whose right-hand side comes from odml.cache_update, or that has a scale attribute or rhs_cache_update, into an FC-form node with external weights: a query-key product (is_src false) is bounded by dst_end_ch_index 2 with K weights in layout kOSpatialIOGroupO4I4, a probability-value product (is_src true) by src_end_ch_index 2 with layout kOSpatialIOGroupI4O4, and INT8 caches become kUint8 weights with a per-channel scale filled from the cache composite's scale_k or scale_v.

An odml.runtime_bmm without a quantized or cache-update right-hand side goes to GpuModelBuilder::BatchedMatMul (transpose_right); E4B's graphs have no such node, since their K and V caches are INT8 outputs of odml.cache_update.

sources.detail: decode composites: odml.cache_update 24 with scale_k/scale_v; KV inputs INT8

text: LiteRT's runtime_bmm kernel builder passes kUint8 K/V weights to GpuModelBuilder::FullyConnectedInt8ExternalWeights with a scale tensor but no weight sums (sum_i), so attention products never take ML Drift's INT8-activation convolution path: they run as FullyConnected up to 16 rows and as a floating-point convolution above.

LiteRT-LM's FillSingleBufferCacheParamTensor zeroes param_tensor and writes {start_index, end_index, end_index}: entry 0 is the position of the run's first new token, entry 1 the end used by add_values_to_cache, entry 2 the end channel used by runtime_batched_matmul.

Our LiteRT pass FuseBoundedAttentionSoftmax (agello-next, LiteRT ede28c641b) rewrites each runtime_bmm(Q, K) -> SELECT_V2(mask, scores, c) [-> MAXIMUM -> MINIMUM] -> SOFTMAX -> runtime_bmm(P, V) tail: the select becomes agello_bounded_mask (logits first, so ML Drift fuses it into the query-key product), the softmax becomes agello_bounded_softmax_reduce over channels [0, params[2]), and the value product reads the masked logits with the reduction as its src_exp input.

text: Our LiteRT delegate reads AGELLO_BOUNDED_ATTENTION once per process (any value starting with 0 turns the bounded-attention rewrite off) and AGELLO_BOUNDED_WINDOW the same way (0 turns off only the local-layer window); ApplyCustomTransformations runs the rewrite when BoundedAttentionEnabled() is true.

Our FindSlidingWindow takes the window W from every LOGICAL_AND(GREATER_EQUAL(p, keys), LESS(p, keys + W)) in the graph whose keys and keys + W are INT32 constants, and gives no window unless all of them agree; Gemma 4 E4B's configuration sets sliding_window 512.

sources.detail: text_config.sliding_window: 512 (google/gemma-4-E4B-it @ ee0ef602)

text: Our bounded-attention rewrite applies the window only to tails whose runtime_bmm composite has is_global = false: the query-key product gets dst_window, the probability-value product src_window and the softmax reduction a start, all with window_pos_index 0 (the run's first position) and window_size W; our runtime_bmm parser keeps is_global for this.

Our ML Drift RuntimeWindowStartSlice (ML Drift 6ae7c68) starts a window at slice (max(0, params[window_pos_index] - (W - 1)) / 32) x 8, that is at channel max(0, p0 - W + 1) rounded down to a multiple of 32 keys, the same in every kernel.
formula: kChannelsAlignment = 32 channels = 8 slices of 4; start_slice = floor(max(0, p0 - W + 1) / 32) * 8; for E4B W = 512

text: ConvRuntimeCheckDesc::HasValues counts window_pos_index, and its comment states that kernels without the window compute every channel, which stays correct while keys below the window are masked.

Our window in ML Drift's FullyConnected kernel (ML Drift 6ae7c68), active when window_pos_index is set and the weights are neither block-quantized nor packed in groups: a probability-value product starts its reduction at the window's first slice, and in a query-key product the threads whose output slice lies below the window run no reduction, leaving the fused mask's epilogue to write the mask value.

text: Our window in ML Drift's Softmax and Softmax1x1 kernels (ML Drift 6ae7c68): with window_pos_index set, the reduction loop starts at RuntimeWindowStartSlice instead of slice 0.

Our window in ConvAppleMPP (ML Drift 2184a7f) is active only when the kernel tiles K itself (manual_k_tiling: a source end bound, manual source reading, or in-kernel I4O4 weight conversion) with 1x1 kernels and no packed groups; a probability-value product then starts its K loop at the window's first slice and a query-key product runs no K iterations for output tiles wholly below it.

On Apple10 GPUs, E4B's prefill query-key products do not use the window: they run ConvAppleMPP with FP16-converted K weights, a DHWBCC4 buffer source and no source end bound, so manual_k_tiling is false; only the probability-value products, whose softmax input forces manual source reading, skip keys below the window.

text: LiteRT's add_values_to_cache kernel writes FP16/FP32 K and V into a uint8 cache by clamping to [-128 x scale, 127 x scale], subtracting the minimum, multiplying by 1 / scale and rounding, so each byte holds the INT8 value plus 128.

LiteRT's add_values_to_cache kernel writes token X of a run at cache index params[0] + X and skips it when that index reaches cache_size or params[1]; with is_ring_buffer it instead writes at (params[0] + X) mod cache_size for X below params[3].

add_values_to_cache writes the K cache in the OSpatialIOGroupO4I4 layout (outputs = tokens) and the V cache in OSpatialIOGroupI4O4 (inputs = tokens), one byte per element; the delegate types quantized cache outputs as kUint8.

LiteRT's op selector adds add_values_to_cache as a GPU operation named add_values_to_cache that allows an input reorder to be fused into it; no node of that name appears in the E4B kernel tables, which count fused nodes under their first operation.

text: GpuModelBuilder::SoftmaxReduce writes a 4-channel tensor per row and uses the Softmax kernel when there are at least 4 rows per compute unit and Softmax1x1 otherwise; GpuModelBuilder::Softmax splits into a reduction and an elementwise pass at 256 or more rows per compute unit.
ML Drift's softmax reduction keeps a running maximum and sum in FP32, rescaling the sum when the maximum grows, and the reduce-only form writes (1 / sum, max) in the destination type.

With our bounded-attention rewrite, E4B's graphs have one 'softmax (reduce)' node per attention (42 in decode and verify, 23 in each prefill graph, 4 in mtp_drafter) and no 'softmax (elementwise)' node, on every Apple family measured.

text: On Metal, ML Drift's elementwise SIN and COS compute sin(x) and cos(x) in the tensor's own type (native_sin/native_cos only on OpenCL Adreno), and its CAST kernel converts to the destination tensor's type.

At LiteRT-LM's default FP16 activations on the GPU (CalculationsPrecision kF16), the tensors that carry E4B's rotary angles (the CAST of the INT32 position, its products and their SIN and COS) are FP16 on the GPU although they are FLOAT32 in the file, and FP16 represents integers exactly only up to 2,048.
formula: FP16 has an 11-bit significand: every integer up to 2^11 = 2,048 is exact, spacing 2 above it
conflicts_with: Run A brief for area A5 (_work task text): 'RoPE (FP32 angles from INT32 positions)'

text: ML Drift's dedicated RoPE kernels (CreateRoPE, CreateSplitRoPEConcat) read the position as float and compute the timescale, angle, sine and cosine in FP32, converting only the results to the tensor type; they serve RoPE operations from composites such as custom_call.rotary_positional_embedding, which E4B's graphs don't contain.

E4B's five GPU graphs contain no embedding_lookup node: on platforms other than Android, LiteRT-LM compiles the text embedder with the CPU accelerator, and the GPU graphs take embeddings and per-layer embeddings as FLOAT32 inputs; ML Drift's GpuModelBuilder::EmbeddingLookup kernel is not used for E4B on Apple.

text: ML Drift derives its Apple family from the GPU name: A14 and M1-series are Apple7, A15, A16 and M2-series Apple8, A17 Pro, A18, A18 Pro, M3- and M4-series Apple9, and A19, A19 Pro, A20 Pro, M5-series and M6 Apple10.

Our ML Drift commit ef08a67 makes GetGpuInfoFromDeviceDescription build AppleInfo from AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU (for example 'Apple A17 Pro') when it is set and non-empty, so family and core-count decisions follow that GPU while the arithmetic stays the real device's.

text: E4B's prefill weight products run in different arithmetic by family: on Apple10, INT8 weights (INT4 converted to INT8) times activations quantized per token to INT8, accumulated in INT32 and dequantized in FP32; on Apple7 to Apple9, FP16 activations times FP16 or directly read INT4/INT8 weights in simdgroup-matrix products accumulated in FP16; decode and verify use the same FullyConnected kernel (FP16 accumulation at kF16) on every family.

text: agello_bounded_mask is an elementwise GPU operation with the logits as first input that writes mask ? logits (clamped when the tail had MAXIMUM/MINIMUM capping) : mask_value, so ML Drift can link it into the producer of the logits.
Our delegate builds agello_bounded_softmax_reduce through GpuModelBuilder::SoftmaxReduce with a SoftmaxRuntimeCheckDesc carrying end_ch_index and, for local layers, window_pos_index and window_size.
LiteRT's runtime_bmm kernel builder copies window_pos_index, window_size, dst_window and src_window from the composite's attributes into ML Drift's ConvRuntimeCheckDesc.

ML Drift's Metal InferenceContext::EncodeWithCommandBuffer encodes every node of the GPU graph on each run, skipping only nodes whose optional tags are disabled, so weights_convert nodes in a prefill graph run on every prefill run.

On an Apple M6 at a 32K window, E4B's digit-copy fidelity cases were exact on both the native Apple10 paths and the simulated Apple9 (A17 Pro) paths: 70 of 70 copies each (runtime build 9b615e492663: ML Drift 2184a7f and LiteRT 97e06d36 with local changes, before ML Drift 15fa9e2).
